title: Tracking issue for document.open() overhaul

labels.name: interop
labels.description: Implementations are not interoperable with each other

body:
This is a list of issues that currently surround `document.open()` interoperability. The list is tentative, and will most probably be extended in the future. For items in the list without dedicated issues or pull requests, I will be filing them individually in the future if need be.

The goal is for each listed issue to have extensive WPT coverage, as well as a confirmed resolution, either as a spec change or "known browser bug; will fix", or both. For now, the "resolution" present is what I believe to be the right path forward, and does not represent the final verdict.

The first checkbox represents if the resolution and tests have been completed. The second represents if the spec change has been submitted (or if it's not necessary).

- [x] ☑️ Order of bail-outs (https://crbug.com/875735, https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/pull/12240, https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/pull/12627, https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/pull/12645)
      **Resolution:** No change to spec required. There seems to be internal bugs in Chrome, Firefox, and Safari.
- [x] ☑️ Return value should be `document` (https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/pull/12359)
      **Resolution:** No change to spec required. Edge returns `null` instead currently, but making Edge return `document` has minimal compatibility risk. Tests needed though.
- [x] ☑️ Calling `document.open()` from custom elements constructor (https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/pull/12037)
      **Resolution:** Keep existing spec in alignment with Chrome and Firefox <ins>and [also Safari](https://trac.webkit.org/changeset/234680/webkit)</ins>. <del>There is an [existing issue](https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=187319) with Safari.</del>
- [x] ☑️ Calling `document.open()` when the `Document` is being unloaded (https://crbug.com/583586, https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/pull/12240, https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/pull/12413)
      **Resolution:** Keep existing spec in alignment with Firefox and Safari. File bugs with (and [fix!](https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/c/chromium/src/+/1169320)) Chrome and (later) Edge.
- [x] ☑️ Non-active documents (#2827, https://crbug.com/741071, https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/pull/12636, https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/pull/12662, https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/pull/12770, **#3977**)
      **Resolution:** Aim to support non-active documents, but defer until other clean-ups are done.
- [x] ☑️ Bail with active parser (https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1475000, https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/pull/11929)
      **Resolution:** No change to spec required. There seems to be a bug in Firefox and Edge.
- [x] ☑️ Stripping out fragments in document URL (#2555, https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/pull/10817, **#3970**)
      **Resolution:** Strip out fragments in document URL in `document.open()` if the entry settings object's document is not the same as the document on which `open()` is called. Align with Chrome (and Edge to a lesser extent, as it strips document URL's fragment in all cases), and provide a simpler but reasonable fix to the scrolling bug.
- [x] ☑️ Aborting document and fetches (#3651, #3975, https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/pull/10789, **#3999**)
      **Resolution:** Only abort when there is an ongoing attempt to navigate. Use the "ideal 2" plan in #3975.
- [x] ☑️ "Prompt to unload" and "unload" (#3286, #3306, https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/pull/10773, https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/pull/10778, **#3918**)
      **Resolution:** Remove "prompt to unload" and "unload" and align with Chrome and Safari. Firefox only fires `beforeunload` but not `pagehide` or `unload` events. Edge doesn't fire any events but still seems to run these steps – which for our purposes is identical to not running them.
- [x] ☑️ Removal of event listeners (https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/pull/12122, https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/pull/12770, **#3893**, **#3977**)
      **Resolution:** Keep existing spec and remove event listeners on document's nodes. Additionally, align with Chrome and Safari in removing event listeners from `Window`, which has minimal compatibility risk due to current Edge and Firefox behaviors of removing tasks (since most events fired on `Window` are fired from tasks).
- [x] ☑️ Removal of event _handlers_ (https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/3836, https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/pull/12122, **#3893**)
      **Resolution:** Set event handlers' values to null (deactivate all event handlers), but do not explicitly remove event handler content attributes. There's no reason to keep handlers there when the underlying event listener has been removed.
- [x] ☑️ Removal of tasks (#3665, https://crbug.com/592867, https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/pull/10818, **#3918**)
      **Resolution:** Do not remove any tasks and align with Chrome, Safari, and partially Firefox.
- [x] ☑️ MutationObserver (https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/pull/12879)
      **Resolution:** No changes to spec required. Continue to make MutationObserver work with `document.open()`'s changes to the DOM tree. The provided test passes in Chrome, Firefox, and Safari, but fails in Edge currently.
- [x] ☑️ Creating a new JavaScript realm (#1698, https://crbug.com/149785, https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/pull/10815, https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/pull/12882, **#3918**)
      **Resolution:** Remove the abstract operation call as well as related steps; dramatically simplify algorithm and align with Chrome and Safari.
- [x] ☑️ Quirks mode (#3831, https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/pull/10679, **#3966**)
      **Resolution:** Align with Chrome, Edge, and Safari and set the document's mode to no-quirks mode in document open steps.
- [x] ☑️ Reload override buffer (#3885, https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=556002, https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/pull/12555, https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/pull/12885, **#3946**)
      **Resolution:** Align with Chrome and Safari, and remove the reload override buffer concept. Align with Safari in following the `Document`'s URL when reloading. Also change the session history entry's URL to be the new `Document`'s URL by using `history.replaceState()` model.
- [x] ☑️ `load` event in conjunction with `document.close()` (https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/pull/10239)
      **Resolution:** This seems to be a bit out of scope for an investigation focused on `document.open()`, as it touches navigation as well as `iframe` loading behavior. Keep existing spec for now, and revisit in the future in the context of a comprehensive `iframe` investigation.
- [x] ☑️ Readiness (https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/pull/10844, https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/pull/12727)
      **Resolution:** Browsers all seem fairly aligned (on `document.open()`'s behavior at least). No need to change spec.
- [x] ☑️ History and replacement (#3564, #3651, #3885, https://crbug.com/68833, https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/pull/12634, https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/pull/12650, **#3946**)
      **Resolution:** Align with Chrome, Safari, and Edge in not adding a history entry when `document.open()` is called – i.e., always use the `replace` semantics. Simplifies implementation and align with Chrome, Safari, and Edge. Also remove `replace` parameter in the process as it's always enabled.
